chunks: The sunnah (prophetic tradition) is that you carry the bier from its four sides, and whatever carrying is done beyond that is voluntary.
As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Mūsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn, who said:

I wrote to him asking him about the bier of the deceased: when it is carried, is there a particular side from its four sides from which one should begin carrying, or may a man carry from whichever side is easier for him, from any side he wishes? So he wrote: “From whichever of them he wishes.”

Thus, the proper understanding of this narration is the lifting of restriction from one who takes up the جنازة from whichever of its sides he wishes, because what we mentioned is from what is recommended in the sunnah, not from what is obligatory.

key_terms.الْجَنَازَةَ: the funeral bier or funeral procession
key_terms.الْمَسْنُونِ: that which is established as sunnah and recommended
key_terms.اَلسَّرِيرَ: the bier or funeral couch of the deceased
key_terms.تَطَوُّعٌ: a voluntary act beyond the established recommendation

ai.seo_question: Is there a prescribed side from which to begin carrying the bier in Islamic funeral practice?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the etiquette and legal status of carrying the bier of the deceased. It explains that carrying it from all four sides is the sunnah (prophetic tradition), but beginning from any particular side is not obligatory, and one may carry it from whichever side one wishes.
